tagline: Through a copper mine, then up into the forest by hairpin.
intro: From Clifton on the San Francisco River the road climbs the Chase Creek valley, doubles back on a hairpin and runs straight through the Morenci mine, three short tunnels included, on a designation that has been temporary since 1974. Past the mine it enters the Apache-Sitgreaves forest and winds north by Hannagan Meadow and Alpine to Springerville and Eagar.

The route roughly follows Coronado's of 1540 to 1542. For decades it was US 666, the sixth branch of Route 66. People thought of the Book of Revelation, the signs kept disappearing, and the highway became US 191.

moments.title: Morenci Mine
moments.text: It began underground in 1871 with mules pulling the ore carts and went to open pit in 1937. Now the highway passes through it, and its owner owns the town of Morenci too.

moments.title: Hannagan Meadow
moments.text: Local legend says Robert Hannagan was chained to a tree here until his son paid off his $1,200 debt. The son paid, and the name stuck.

moments.title: Alpine
moments.text: Mormon settlers named it for its height, 8,050 feet, and as of 1960 it was the highest place in the country where farming was carried on with success.

practical: North of the mine the road through the forest has no shoulders and many hairpin turns along steep mountainsides.
